---
title: "AutoFloods"
---

## Overview

AutoFloods lets you map flooded areas from Sentinel-1 SAR (radar)
imagery over any region and time period you choose. Give it an area of
interest and a date range, and it returns a flood extent for every
scene it finds, plus a monthly count of how often each pixel was
flooded. The software's focus is on what it takes to run that
unattended at scale: memory optimization, parallelization,
end-to-end pipeline orchestration, and, above all, modularity, so that
a different data source or a different detection algorithm can be
plugged in without touching the rest of the pipeline.

Under the hood, floods are detected by per-pixel Z-score anomaly
detection: a dry-season VV/VH backscatter baseline (mean and standard
deviation, in decibels) is fit for every pixel, and a wet-season scene
is flagged flooded wherever its backscatter drops well below that
baseline, with a terrain-slope mask to suppress false positives on
steep ground. The algorithm is the one behind Global Flood Mapper; you
can read its details and validation in
[Tripathy and Malladi (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-022-05428-2).
However, AutoFloods also lets you integrate your own flood detection
algorithm in place of it, through the same `FloodDetector` interface
the built-in detector uses.

The workflow is tiled by design: each AOI is processed as its own
independent unit rather than one large country- or state-scale mosaic,
so a run over any number of tiles scales by adding more of the same
unit of work -- see `flood_mapper` in the
[API reference](reference/index.qmd) for the per-tile pipeline this
drives.

## Data sources

AutoFloods reads Sentinel-1 RTC (radiometrically terrain corrected)
imagery through a pluggable `STACSource` interface, with two
implementations:

- **`MPCSource`** -- Microsoft Planetary Computer, the original backend.
- **`OPERASource`** -- NASA's OPERA RTC-S1 product via ASF/CMR, hosted on
  AWS. Native 30m resolution.

Swap between them (or add a new source) via the `source=` argument to
`flood_mapper` -- see [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

## Installation

```bash
pip install --pre autofloods
```

For contributors working from a local clone:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

See `pyproject.toml` for the pinned dependency list. `MPCSource` needs no
credentials at all; `OPERASource` requires a NASA Earthdata Login entry
in `~/.netrc`. See [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd#authentication)
for setup steps.

**System dependency for `OPERASource`**: mosaicking uses the GDAL
command-line tools (`gdalbuildvrt`), which `pip install` does **not**
provide -- `rasterio`'s pip wheel bundles its own GDAL library
internally but doesn't expose the CLI binaries. Install them
separately:

```bash
# Debian/Ubuntu, or Google Colab
apt-get install -y gdal-bin

# conda/mamba (any platform)
conda install -c conda-forge gdal
```

See [gdal.org/download.html](https://gdal.org/download.html) for other
platforms. `MPCSource` does not need this. If `gdalbuildvrt` is missing,
`OPERASource` raises a clear error pointing back here rather than a raw
`FileNotFoundError`.

## Citation

If you use this package (or part of it), please cite:

> Tripathy, P., & Malladi, T. (2022). Global Flood Mapper: a novel Google
> Earth Engine application for rapid flood mapping using Sentinel-1 SAR.
> *Natural Hazards*, 114(2), 1341-1363.
> <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-022-05428-2>

> Tripathy, P., Malladi, T., Balakrishnan, K., & Parath, N. (n.d.).
> *AutoFloods: A Python package for automated flood mapping at scale
> using Sentinel-1 SAR* [Manuscript in preparation].
